There's a couple of really phenomenal physics/sciences related sites I enjoy:

  • http://www.feynmanlectures.caltech.edu/ - Richard Feynman's lecture series at Caltech. It's mostly physics but interweaves with everything. The thing I really like about them is that somehow the lectures are in no way dumbed down, yet they're also simultaneously extremely accessible for anybody with a shade of self motivation and access to a search engine!

  • http://theoreticalminimum.com/home - An awesome collection of series upon series of physics lectures from Leonard Susskind. There's courses on everything from classical mechanics to modern string theory and more. I would not recommend clicking on the link on that page, "What Worries Me Most." I've watched at this point likely hundreds of hours of videos from the man and he's never even once hinted at what that video gets into it which is, predictably, politics. That was disappointing and completely out of character - in any case it does not affect his competence or eloquence in education.

Susskind also has a book by the same name, "The Theoretical Minimum", available. It assumes you have some background in math/science (for instance basic calculus is reviewed, but not taught) but are a bit 'out of the loop.' Can't say enough positive about that.
